obtained.how: the blog post on the Vermont Center for Ecostudies' own web site

bibliography.note: 'The Ripple Effect: Wakeboats Pose Risks to Loon Nests', August 6, 2025, by Emily Anderson, Vermont Center for Ecostudies blog. Matches.

claims.claim: Loon nests are typically 5–20 cm above the water
claims.source_value: two to eight inches (5.1–20.3 cm) above the water level, on shorelines or nesting rafts
claims.location: web page, paragraph beginning 'The challenges of enforcing these buffer zones'
claims.quote: usually located two to eight inches above the water level
claims.conditions: Vermont; a conservation organisation's blog post, no source given for the figure

claims.claim: a motorboat passing at 15 m raises a wave of about 13–15 cm
claims.source_value: a standard motorboat 50 ft (15.2 m) away produces a wave five to six inches (12.7–15.2 cm) tall, given as the equivalent of a wakeboat at 500 ft
claims.location: web page, paragraph beginning 'Despite the new rule’s stricter guidelines'
claims.quote: motorboat would from just 50 feet away, producing a wave five to six inches tall
claims.conditions: blog post; no measurement or source cited; wave height not defined (crest to trough or above still water)
claims.note: 50 ft = 15.2 m; 5–6 in = 12.7–15.2 cm. The rewrite might say it is an unsourced statement in an advocacy blog.

notes: Also: wakeboats closer than 500 ft 'could produce waves in excess of eight to ten inches'; Vermont's 2024 wakesport zones were at least 50 contiguous acres, 500 ft from shore, 20 ft deep and 200 ft wide, a proposed rule raising the minimum to 100 acres with a 500-ft buffer around loon nests. No nest locations are given.
